result.summary: The record holds ONE owner sentence that opens a Scribe subscription tier — 2026-09-14 ~13:2x, "Because I'm thinking that this could actually be a new paid subscription tier in and of itself" — and it is a THOUGHT, not a signature. Everything else about the Scribe's economics is the chair's own, recorded vetoably under the 09-13 total-delegation grant, and every one of it is INERT: `dossierProse: 5` credits sits in `pricing.js` behind `FLAGS.scribe = false`, migration 202 is written and NOT applied, and the owner's five acts (the key · `db push` 201+202 · the tier's price and shape · item 13 · the flag) are all outstanding. The design's §12 owner-gated list runs 1–15; §11c points at "§12 item 16, the tier" — AN ITEM THAT WAS NEVER WRITTEN. There is no tier proposal anywhere in the record: no price, no entitlement shape, no render allowance, no cap. Three facts should drive the proposal. (1) The 13:2x amendment removed the Scribe from the free AND paid subscription product entirely — the corpus is every subscription's prose until the rewrite is finished — so the tier is additive, not a repricing. (2) The chair's 5-credit default is worth $0.65–$1.00 at shipped retail pack rates, and my arithmetic over the MEASURED RUN-5 prompt puts one epoch render at roughly $0.73–$1.32 of Opus 5 COGS excluding adaptive-thinking output — i.e. the per-render SKU is at or below cost at the best pack rate. (3) The design's own cost paragraph (§6: "a few tens of thousands of input tokens per settlement … cents per settlement on Opus 5, not dollars") PREDATES the prompt that now ships: the measured cached prefix alone is ~28 K tokens read on every one of ~10 tab calls, ~390 K input tokens per settlement for the writer alone and the same again for the tier-1 reader. That paragraph is the single largest unmeasured part of the design, and the design says so itself ("to be MEASURED in the pilot, not trusted"). Also: the "daily render cap (three saves, one render a day)" that the 08:5x memory calls a temporary economics EXISTS NOWHERE ELSE — not in the design, not in the rulings, not in code; `saveLimit: 3` is the Wanderer tier's save cap, and the chair appears to have read a render cap into it. The closest precedent for the tier's shape is SURVEYOR_PLAN ($14.99/mo, `monthlyCredits: 0` as a dial, BYOK, an ENTITLEMENT rather than a `TIERS` key) — deliberately outside `TIERS` so `getVisibleTiers()` stays three-way.

facts.topic: Owner directive — the tier (the ONLY statement that opens it)
facts.fact: VERBATIM, 2026-09-14 ~13:2x, AMENDING the 08:5x frame: "okay then with that, i ammend what i said before. the scribe is the AI narrative layer/overlay. Free and paid subscription generation uses the full corpus only until the full rewrite is finished. I still want you to continnue the scribe work to completion however. Because I'm thinking that this could actually be a new paid subscription tier in and of itself". Note the modality — "I'm thinking that this COULD actually be". It licenses the proposal; it signs nothing.

facts.topic: Owner directive — what 13:2x SUPERSEDED
facts.fact: The memory records the amendment as striking, explicitly: the 08:5x frame (Scribe as the intermediate for cash flow), "the Scribe as the DEFAULT render for the product, the once-a-day render cap as temporary economics, the per-render credit SKU as the Scribe's price, the free first render (chair ruling 2). Those are now design inputs for a SUBSCRIPTION TIER, not the free/paid product's defaults." So ruling 1's 5-credit SKU and ruling 2's free first render are NO LONGER the product's defaults — they are raw material for the tier design and must be re-decided inside it.

facts.topic: Owner directive — how 13:2x says to apply it
facts.fact: VERBATIM from the same memory's How-to-apply: "`FLAGS.scribe` stays false for every tier until the tier exists; no Scribe render is ever the default for free or paid subscribers; W4/W5 design the Scribe as a SUBSCRIPTION entitlement (an account tier gate at `scribe-render`, replacing or wrapping the per-render credit spend) — a paid-surface design that is the owner's to sign; the daily cap and the free first render are re-decided inside that design." The word ENTITLEMENT is the chair's read, and it is the same word the shipped Surveyor plan uses.

facts.topic: Owner directive — the end state (08:5x, still standing)
facts.fact: VERBATIM 2026-09-14 ~08:5x: "Quite the opposite. The corpus prose is the hopeful final version because then it unlocks every free version to truly be free. The AI is the intermediate to get something workable and to get cash flow so I can keep working on the prose." And, same hour: "when the corpus is done, the AI is going to move to a higher tier for payment." The 13:2x amendment struck the INTERMEDIATE half; this second sentence — the Scribe as a higher paid tier once the corpus lands — is what 13:2x brought forward and made immediate rather than eventual.

facts.topic: Owner directive — the chair's own gloss on the end state
facts.fact: The chair recorded (not the owner's words): "So W5's paid surface is designed as a TIER feature from the start (a Surveyor-like entitlement with renders bundled), with per-credit metering only as the intermediate's bridge; the price row and the tier are owner-signed." This is the only place in the record where a tier SHAPE is named, and it is the chair's proposal, dated 09-14 ~08:5x, written before the 13:2x amendment.
facts.where: same file, THE END STATE paragraph

facts.topic: THE DAILY CAP DOES NOT EXIST
facts.fact: The sentence "The free tier's daily render cap (three saves, one render a day) is a TEMPORARY economics of the intermediate" appears in exactly ONE place in the whole record — that memory file. It is absent from the design doc, absent from SCRIBE-RULINGS (all 36), and absent from the code: greps for daily cap / renders per day / DAILY_LIMIT across src/ and supabase/functions/scribe-render return only the ANONYMOUS GENERATION cap (HomeHero.jsx:442 `DEFAULT_DAILY_CAP`) and the BYOK key caps. "Three saves" is `TIERS.wanderer.saveLimit: 3`. No Scribe render cap was ever designed, ruled or built; the chair appears to have narrated one from the save limit.

facts.topic: Owner directive — the billing unit (the render trigger)
facts.fact: VERBATIM 2026-09-14 ~06:3x: "but generation happens only once a settlement's dossier is opened and frozen until next advance time." Read into the design as: nothing renders on save or on advance by itself; an advance only makes the artefact stale; the next OPEN of that settlement's dossier renders; "A settlement never opened in an epoch is never rendered and never billed — in a realm of thirty towns advanced a year, only the ones the game master looks at are scribed." This is the load-bearing economics of any tier: the billable unit is opened-settlement × epoch, not settlement and not advance.
facts.where: ruling 14, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §5 CREATE and §5b THE TRIGGER IS THE OPEN

facts.topic: Owner directive — the advance rule (what makes a render recur)
facts.fact: VERBATIM 2026-09-14 ~06:1x: "new rule. when advance time happens, the program reads teh new town card, the history of town cards, and what happened last. or however we have it now. This is essentially the narrative overlay set as default and without prose already constructed for it to refine. so think of it like that in terms of how it reads past settlements data to make things remain coherent." Consequence for the tier: the artefact is write-once PER EPOCH, so a campaign advanced twelve times over a year bills up to twelve renders per settlement the DM actually opens. Design §5b: "The pilot (§10) measures a 12-advance campaign end to end, not only epoch 0."
facts.where: ruling 13, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §5b including its COST bullet

facts.topic: Owner directive — what else is billed (REDO)
facts.fact: VERBATIM 2026-09-14 ~06:5x, among four product rules: "and there should be an option to redo the AI narrative, to redraw based on the current settlement's facts. lastly, remove the Narrative overlay option because it is now redundant. But do key in the AI instructions box in the dossier to be additional instructions that is actually read and used by the AI for the prose for the dossier. And lastly, with this, it is automatially default that the daily life tab be populated rather than on command. let's just get it all out there." Ruling 16 reads REDO as "billed per render"; ruling 18 makes editing the AI-instructions box REDO-ELIGIBLE but never an automatic render. So a DM who edits guidance and redraws pays again — a second billable event the tier design must price or absorb.

facts.topic: Owner directive — the retirements that fund the SKU
facts.fact: The same 06:5x order retires the narrative overlay AND (ruling 19) daily life's on-command button: "DAILY LIFE renders by default as the seventh tab call of every epoch render … its on-command button and SKU retire. Ruling 1 AMENDED: one render SKU, chair's default 5 credits (the retired narrative's), owner-signed." So the Scribe's SKU is priced AT the SKU it replaces, and two existing SKUs (`narrative: 5`, `dailyLife: 4`) go away — revenue the tier must replace, not add to.
facts.where: ruling 19, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §5c rules 2 and 4, and the "Owner-gated item 14 (recorded)" note after §5c

facts.topic: Chair ruling 1 (as amended by 19) — THE PRICE
facts.fact: Ruling 1 first set `dossierProse: 4` credits "between narrative 5 and dailyLife 4"; ruling 19 amended it to "one render SKU, chair's default 5 credits (the retired narrative's), owner-signed." Rationale on the record: "priced like the feature it most resembles; the pilot's measured COGS re-prices it before launch." `TIER_MULTIPLIERS` left untouched because "all-1 is the owner-signed activation switch." The re-pricing the ruling promises has never happened — the pilot has never run.

facts.topic: The price row AS BUILT
facts.fact: `NEW_AI_COSTS` carries `dossierProse: 5` with the comment: "⭐ THE SCRIBE'S ONE RENDER SKU (chair ruling 1 as amended by ruling 19; migration 202's `spend_credits` arm is the server mirror). ONE PRICE FOR A WHOLE RENDER of a settlement's dossier — every tab AND the daily-life beats, per epoch — set at the retired narrative's own five credits. INERT: nothing spends this feature until FLAGS.scribe is lit, which is an owner act." `FAST_AI_COSTS` carries the same 5 deliberately, "so `getAiCostForModel('dossierProse', anyPreference)` answers the true price instead of `undefined`" — there is no cheaper model tier to price because ruling 8 fixed one model.

facts.topic: What a credit is worth (the retail anchor for the SKU)
facts.fact: Shipped `NEW_PACKS`: credits_25 $4.99 → $0.20/credit; credits_60 $9.99 → $0.17/credit; credits_150 $19.99 → $0.13/credit. A 5-credit render therefore retails at $1.00 / $0.85 / $0.65 depending on which pack the user bought. This is the ceiling any per-render tier economics has to clear.

facts.topic: The shipped subscription ladder (what a Scribe tier would sit beside)
facts.fact: `TIERS`: wanderer — $0/forever, `saveLimit: 3`, no pdf/json export, `maxSize: 'capital'`. cartographer — `priceCents: 599` ($5.99/mo, "reconciled to the displayed price (owner sign-off 2026-07-17)"), `monthlyCredits: 30`, unlimited saves, all exports. founder — lifetime, NO SKU ("A chair is given, never sold"), `oneTimeCredits: 30`, seatLimit 30. Plus `SINGLE_DOSSIER` at `priceCents: 299` ($2.99, claimable without signup). At 5 credits a render, Cartographer's 30 monthly credits buy SIX renders a month.

facts.topic: THE PRECEDENT for a Scribe tier — SURVEYOR_PLAN
facts.fact: `SURVEYOR_PLAN`: `priceCents: 1499` ($14.99/mo, "§464.2 ruled the band $14.99–19.99 at its floor"), `billing: 'monthly'`, `monthlyCredits: 0`, `byok: true`, `entitlement: 'surveyor_entitlements'`. Its header is the architectural ruling a Scribe tier should copy or consciously break: "NOT a `TIERS` key, deliberately. `TIERS` keys are `profiles.tier` shapes, and Surveyor is an ENTITLEMENT (`surveyor_entitlements`, migration 139) rather than a billing tier — the same reason 139 declined to widen the tier CHECK. Keeping it outside `TIERS` is what lets `getVisibleTiers()` stay three-way and leaves every existing TIERS consumer untouched." Its `monthlyCredits: 0` is documented as "THE DIAL — WEB-10 sets it when the webhook can grant", i.e. the allowance is minted by the Stripe webhook, which does not know about the constant yet. A Scribe tier with bundled renders inherits exactly that unbuilt granting path.

facts.topic: The activation switch is owner-signed
facts.fact: `TIER_MULTIPLIERS` is `{scout: 1, journeyman: 1, master: 1}` with the comment: "⚠ EVERY VALUE HERE IS 1 ON PURPOSE. This map is the ACTIVATION SWITCH for the quoted price, and pricing activation is owner-signed (design §5; owner queue M5, the pricing-sheet sign-off) … Changing a number here without the owner's signature silently reprices a paid surface." Any tier proposal that scales price by capability tier touches this map and therefore needs the owner's pricing-sheet signature, not just a tier sign-off.

facts.topic: Chair ruling 2 — THE FREE FIRST RENDER
facts.fact: "FREE FIRST RENDER — YES, one per ACCOUNT on the migration-118 pattern (`claim_free_scribe`), released on failure. RATIONALE: the same product logic as the free first narrative; unfarmable by construction." Built into migration 202 as a conditional UPDATE whose `found` is the answer. The 13:2x amendment explicitly puts this back on the table: "the daily cap and the free first render are re-decided inside that design." So ruling 2 is BUILT but no longer decided.

facts.topic: Migration 202 — written, NOT applied
facts.fact: Header verbatim: "⚠️ INERT UNTIL TWO SEPARATE ACTS. Applying this migration changes no existing behaviour: the claim functions have no caller until the Scribe's flag is lit, and the `dossierProse` arm is reachable only from a feature name nothing spends today. `FLAGS.scribe` defaults to FALSE and lighting it is the owner's act; so is `supabase db push`." The SKU arm is added by recreating `spend_credits` from migration 192 VERBATIM with one line — `when 'dossierProse' then 5` — because "`spend_credits` RAISES on an unknown feature, by design, so a new SKU is a new arm or it is a failed spend." Rollback documented: recreate from the 192 body and drop the three claim functions, "Safe at any time while the Scribe's flag is dark."

facts.topic: The flag
facts.fact: `scribe: false` in the flag registry. Its description: "THE SCRIBE: AI-written dossier prose, rendered once per epoch when a settlement's dossier is opened, refuted by the tier-0 instruments, and persisted on the settlement. Default OFF and INERT: with the flag off nothing renders, nothing is billed, no Scribe module enters the first-paint closure, and every tab draws the hand corpus. Lighting it opens a PAID surface, so it needs the render SKU seeded and the provider key in place first."

facts.topic: Chair ruling 10 — BYOK
facts.fact: "BYOK — a BYOK user's Scribe runs on THEIR key at THEIR model's probe tier (the ladder's no-flattening rule), the tier-0 refuter unchanged, the tier-1 refuter on the same model as their writer (the conflicted-witness rule)." Design §8 adds the retention consequence: "the managed path uses Opus 5; BYOK users' model choice inherits their own org's retention — recorded, not decided." For a tier proposal BYOK is the natural zero-COGS arm — and it is the one Surveyor already sells at $14.99/mo with `byok: true` and a zero credit allowance.
facts.where: ruling 10, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §8; SURVEYOR_PLAN byok:true in pricing.js

facts.topic: Chair ruling 8 — MODEL (a cost input)
facts.fact: "MODEL — `claude-opus-5` (the API skill's default) for the writer and the tier-1 refuter on the managed path; adaptive thinking, `effort: 'high'`, structured outputs, streaming, server-side `fallbacks: \"default\"`. A Fable selector arm runs in the PILOT only (design §6) and is adopted only if the blind read prefers it. The `opus-4-8` defaults elsewhere are NOT moved by the Scribe." Note the tension with the shipped `DEFAULT_MODEL_PREFERENCE = 'anthropic_claude_opus_4_8'`: the Scribe runs a model the product's own model-preference UI does not list, so per-user model choice does not reduce its COGS.
facts.where: ruling 8, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §6 Model paragraph; lane-scribe/src/config/pricing.js:160 (DEFAULT_MODEL_PREFERENCE) and :162-227 (AI_MODEL_OPTIONS)

facts.topic: Model choice, measured (the cheaper-tier question is closed for now)
facts.fact: RUN 5: Opus 87 % of pools shipped vs Sonnet 84 %; contradicting lines Opus 6 vs Sonnet 6. RUN 4: Opus 89 / Sonnet 85, contradictions 2 vs 8, FAILs 10 vs 14. RUN 3's ruling 4: "Opus stays the writer; a per-tab Sonnet seat is not supported by this run. Re-open with live usage receipts." So the obvious COGS lever — a cheaper writer — was measured and declined on quality, with re-opening explicitly conditioned on live receipts the programme does not have.
facts.where: SCRIBE-SIM-2026-09-14.md, RUN 3 §4, RUN 4 Model line, RUN 5 table

facts.topic: Chair ruling 3 — the public projection (a distribution, not a price, decision)
facts.fact: "THE PUBLIC PROJECTION — NOT SHOWN to gallery viewers and NOT copied on gallery import in W2 (absent from `PUBLIC_TOPLEVEL_KEYS`; migration 196 adds the claim RPC only). RATIONALE: fail-closed is the estate's rule; showing paid, unrefuted-by-a-human prose on the public gallery is a reversible LATER decision, hiding it is the safe first state. Re-open at W5." A tier that bundles renders should decide whether a subscriber's rendered prose is visible to non-subscribers in the gallery — the re-open is scheduled for exactly the wave the tier lands in.
facts.where: ruling 3, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §5 THE PUBLIC PROJECTION / SQL TWIN and §12 item 3

facts.topic: Chair ruling 7 — re-scribe (a recurring-revenue lever, default OFF)
facts.fact: "RE-SCRIBE — the growth opt-in's shape exactly: a campaign-level, versioned, explicit 're-scribe this world under Scribe vN' that re-renders EVERY block (never a partial mix) and keeps the prior artefact in `versionHistory` as one entry … Default OFF. Nothing re-renders on its own." Under THE PROMISE a world opened under a newer scribeVersion does NOT re-render; only an advance renders a new epoch. So there is no version-churn revenue and no version-churn cost without an explicit campaign opt-in.
facts.where: ruling 7, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §7 second bullet; §12 item 7

facts.topic: Chair ruling 5 — the residual error rate (the tier's quality promise)
facts.fact: "THE RESIDUAL ERROR RATE — the pilot's gate (design §10): ship behind the flag only at or below the corpus's audited defect rate; WITHHELDs ship (the corpus's own rule); FAILs never ship (the unit falls back to the corpus). No number is set by hand." Design §10's proposed decision rule: ships "if its post-refute FAIL rate is at or below the hand corpus's own audited defect rate … AND the blind read prefers it or ties" — and the blind read is specified as "a 40-unit blind read: the owner and one Fable seat." The owner has never sat that read.
facts.where: ruling 5, SCRIBE-RULINGS.md; design §10 including its Decision rule

facts.topic: Owner standard — what the tier actually sells
facts.fact: VERBATIM 2026-09-14 ~14:4x: "okay, to clarify again, the goal is that it doesn't contradict the settlement not that it invents when it comes to prose." Ruling 36 makes this law for both seats and SUPERSEDES ruling 35's six invention bars. This is why the measured ship rate moved from 26 % to 84 %+ in one afternoon — RUN 2's "70 % refused" was a licence reading, not the product.

facts.topic: MEASURED — the shipped share (RUN 5, the current ceiling)
facts.fact: RUN 5 (workflow `wf_00f13b26-496`, dock `f350d7ed5`, 64 seats, 8.9 M tokens, 16 cells = hamlet/village/town/city × defense/economics/overview/power): Opus 198 pools → 188 returned → 178 tier-0 kept → 5 tier-1 dropped → **173 shipped (87 %)**; Sonnet 188 → 172 → 6 → **166 (84 %)**. Contradiction LINES: Opus 6 (field 3 · page 3), Sonnet 6 (field 4 · page 2) — 12 in ~1,400; roster 0, model 0, record 0, forecast 0. The chair's 20:3x ruling: "The Scribe without a key is at its natural ceiling: 84–89 % of pools ship as the Scribe's, ~0.5–0.7 % of lines contradict."

facts.topic: MEASURED — the arc that produced it
facts.fact: Over one afternoon of one 16-cell grid: RUN 2 26 % (Opus) / 30 % (Sonnet) under the licence reading → RUN 3 84 % / 78 % (the owner's non-contradiction standard + the honest card) → RUN 4 89 % / 85 % (the page's machine lines in the writer's turn, `town.bodies`) → RUN 5 87 % / 84 % (the card's reads resolved). RUN 5 is explicitly read as "flat against RUN 4 within the writer's own draw-to-draw variance (the craft withholds swing ±20 between runs of one prompt: Q on Opus 36 → 22 → 41 across RUNS 3–5)" — so 84–89 % is a band, not a point.

facts.topic: MEASURED — the prompt, cached global brief
facts.fact: `brief.md` = **96,795 chars**, BYTE-IDENTICAL across all four seeds (hamlet/village/town/city) and all twelve non-daily-life tabs → ≈24.2 K tokens at ~4.0 chars/token. This is cached block 1, shared by every settlement of the hour. The daily-life tab's brief is **98,480 chars** (the daily-life register section) — a DIFFERENT prefix, therefore a SECOND cache write per hour, which the design's one-cached-brief economics does not account for.

facts.topic: MEASURED — the prompt, cached town block
facts.fact: `town.md` (cached block 2, shared across one settlement's tabs, constant per seed): hamlet (Warmholz) **6,568** · village (Hochhausen) **10,089** · town (Spitzplatz) **15,964** · city (Rundgate) **16,236** chars → ≈1.6 / 2.5 / 4.0 / 4.1 K tokens. The cached prefix a town-tier tab call carries is therefore ≈28.2 K tokens (brief + town).

facts.topic: MEASURED — the prompt, volatile turn, per tab
facts.fact: Spitzplatz (town), all 13 tabs, `turn.md` chars: defense 25,695 · overview 20,772 · power 9,963 · plot_hooks 9,314 · economics 8,420 · history 7,079 · daily_life 5,023 · viability 4,644 · services 2,287 · faith 1,676 · relationships 402 · resources 398 · war 392. **Total 96,065 chars ≈ 24.0 K tokens per settlement.** Across tiers the big four tabs scale: hamlet defense 28,016 / overview 23,380; city defense 30,947 / overview 17,970 — a hamlet's turn is NOT smaller than a city's, because the turn carries the page and the pools, not the town's size.
facts.where: /private/tmp/…/kit/scribe-harness/out/sim/<seed>/<tab>/turn.md; output schema is 740 chars (≈185 tokens) on every tab

facts.topic: MEASURED — the prompt, tier-1 checklist
facts.fact: `tier1-opus.md` chars: defense **36,710** · overview **35,811** · power **26,139** · economics **25,569** = 124,229 chars ≈ 31.1 K tokens over four tabs. NOTE A FIDELITY GAP: the harness's tier-1 prompt is SELF-CONTAINED — it re-embeds "THE TOWN: {armedForces: …}" and the two-ladders / funding-note law inline. Ruling 31 and RUN 3's finding 5 say that in the PRODUCT "the checklist rides under the same cached brief", so the product's tier-1 input is mostly a cache read while the harness's is full-price. Which of the two the built `scribe-render` actually sends has never been measured against the API.

facts.topic: MEASURED — how many calls a render actually makes
facts.fact: The built transport calls `firingTabs(settlement, renderTabPage, SCRIBE_TABS)` and keeps only tabs whose page has a `kind === 'composed'` line: `const tabs = firingTabs(...); if (tabs.length === 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'no-tabs' };`. On Spitzplatz that is ~10 of 13 tabs (war/resources/relationships have ~400-char turns and no pools). `SCRIBE_TABS` is derived from `DOSSIER_MOUNTS`, and `townCard.js:398` records "Over the pinned town's THIRTEEN TABS". The design §6 still says "six tab calls" and §5c rule 4 calls daily life "a SEVENTH TAB CALL" — the design's call count is stale by roughly a factor of 1.7 against the built code.

facts.topic: COST ESTIMATE — the rates
facts.fact: From the claude-api skill (model table cached 2026-06-24): Claude Opus 5 `claude-opus-5`, 1M context, **$5.00 /MTok input, $25.00 /MTok output**; Sonnet 5 $2/$10. Prompt caching: **cache reads ~0.1× base input ($0.50/MTok on Opus 5); cache writes 1.25× for 5-minute TTL, 2× for 1-hour TTL ($10/MTok on Opus 5)**; break-even on a 1h TTL needs at least three requests. Message Batches run **asynchronously at 50 % cost**. The design pins `ttl: '1h'` on the block brief (§3.1) and names the Batches path for unopened worlds (§6, "renders overnight at half price").
facts.where: claude-api skill — Current Models table, shared/prompt-caching.md:144, and the Batches line in the Quick Task Reference; design §3.1 item 1 and §6 Wall-clock

facts.topic: COST ESTIMATE — one epoch render, PLAUSIBLE not confirmed
facts.fact: Arithmetic over the RUN-5 prompt at ~4.0 chars/token (the chair's own RUN-1 ratio: 148,890 chars ≈ 37 K tokens), town tier, ~10 firing tabs, Opus 5 first-party rates. WRITER, cold hour (both brief variants written at the 1h 2× rate): writes 52.8 K ≈ $0.53 + cache reads ≈230 K ≈ $0.12 + volatile turns 23.7 K ≈ $0.12 + visible output ≈6 K ≈ $0.15 ⇒ **≈ $0.92**. WRITER, warm hour (only the town block written): $0.04 + $0.14 + $0.12 + $0.15 ⇒ **≈ $0.45**. TIER-1 READER, 10 calls riding the same cached prefix ⇒ **≈ $0.28–$0.40**. **TOTAL ≈ $0.73 (warm) to $1.32 (cold) per epoch render** — EXCLUDING adaptive-thinking output tokens, which the design pins at `effort: 'high'`, which bill at $25/MTok, and which no artefact on disk measures; a 2–5× multiple on visible output would add $0.15–$0.60. Batches halve the whole figure. Label: PLAUSIBLE (arithmetic over measured chars and published rates), never CONFIRMED — no API call has ever been made.
facts.where: derived from the measured files above + claude-api rates; the chars/token ratio is from SCRIBE-SIM-2026-09-14.md §"The run" ("brief 115,307 chars (cached) + turn 33,583 chars (volatile) ≈ 37 K tokens")

facts.topic: COST — the SKU is at or below COGS
facts.fact: 5 credits retails at $1.00 (25-pack) / $0.85 (60-pack) / $0.65 (150-pack). The estimate above puts one render at ≈$0.73–$1.32 of Opus 5 COGS before thinking tokens, before Stripe's cut, before the free first render, and before any repair round. At the 150-pack rate the chair's default SKU is UNDERWATER; at the 25-pack rate it is roughly break-even. This is the strongest argument in the record for a subscription tier over per-render credits — and it is arithmetic nobody has run before now.
facts.where: pricing.js NEW_PACKS :48-52 and NEW_AI_COSTS :73 against the cost estimate above

facts.topic: THE DESIGN'S COST MODEL IS STALE — the central unmeasured part
facts.fact: Design §6 verbatim: "**Caching and cost, per settlement (to be MEASURED in the pilot, not trusted):** six tab calls; the block brief cached after the first settlement of the hour (`cache_read_input_tokens` is the receipt — the runsheet's 'one economic claim no test can prove', verified by reading it on two consecutive calls); the town card ~3–6 K tokens per tab; the output ~60–70 units × ~40 tokens ≈ 3 K per settlement; the tier-1 refute the same size again. Order of magnitude: a few tens of thousands of input tokens per settlement, mostly cached, and a few thousand output. At the skill's listed first-party rates that is cents per settlement on Opus 5, not dollars — and it is the owner's paid surface, so the price row (§12) is signed, not derived." MEASURED AGAINST THAT: ~10 tab calls not six; a 24.2 K-token cached prefix read on EVERY call ⇒ ~280–370 K cache-read tokens per settlement for the writer alone, plus ~24 K volatile — roughly 390 K input tokens, an order of magnitude above "a few tens of thousands", and the cache reads are 0.1× not free. The §6 paragraph was written before the prompt it prices existed.

facts.topic: WHAT THE SIMULATION CANNOT TELL US (the design says so twice)

facts.topic: Security and retention (constraints on any tier's fine print)
facts.fact: Design §8: player units from the player projection, DM notebook units from the DM read — "**two calls, never one context**". Keys stay server-side; BYOK through the vault ("never logged, fail-closed on vault error per the owner's 2026-07-30 ruling; the probe-tier guard"). "`probeProfile` stays NULL on the managed path so the server key's cached prefix is byte-identical for every user — the block brief must not vary per user either." That last clause is load-bearing economics: a per-user or per-tier brief would destroy the cache sharing the whole cost model rests on, so a tier CANNOT differentiate by prompt content. Ruling 9: "NO Scribe prose enters any training/research corpus without the campaign-level toggle."

openQuestions: THE TIER'S SHAPE IS UNWRITTEN. §11c points at "§12 item 16, the tier" and §12 stops at 15. Is the Scribe tier (a) a fourth `TIERS` key beside wanderer/cartographer/founder, or (b) an ENTITLEMENT outside `TIERS` on the SURVEYOR_PLAN pattern — which pricing.js documents as the deliberate choice that "lets `getVisibleTiers()` stay three-way and leaves every existing TIERS consumer untouched"? Nothing in the record decides this, and it determines whether the tier CHECK constraint has to widen (migration 139 declined to).

WHAT DOES THE TIER METER? The owner's 13:2x how-to-apply says "an account tier gate at `scribe-render`, replacing OR WRAPPING the per-render credit spend" — the chair wrote both options and chose neither. Unlimited renders under a flat fee is uncapped COGS at ~$0.73–$1.32 a render; a bundled allowance keeps `dossierProse: 5` and needs the Stripe webhook to grant, which SURVEYOR_PLAN's `monthlyCredits: 0` docblock says is UNBUILT ("WEB-10 flips the dial in the same commit that teaches the webhook to grant").

IS THE 5-CREDIT SKU SOLVENT? At the 150-pack rate 5 credits is $0.65 against an estimated $0.73–$1.32 of COGS before thinking tokens. Ruling 1 promised "the pilot's measured COGS re-prices it before launch" and the pilot has never run. Should the proposal price the tier off this estimate, or refuse to name a number until the key produces `cache_read_input_tokens` and dollar receipts — which the design itself calls "one economic claim no test can prove"?

HOW MANY RENDERS DOES A REAL MONTH OF PLAY BUY? The billable unit is opened-settlement × epoch, plus every REDO. Nobody has modelled a realistic month: a DM with one campaign of thirty towns advancing monthly and opening six of them bills six renders; a DM who tunes AI guidance and redraws bills more. Cartographer's 30 monthly credits buy exactly six renders today. Without this model, any allowance number is arbitrary.

DOES ADAPTIVE THINKING AT effort:'high' DOUBLE THE BILL? Ruling 8 pins `effort: 'high'` with adaptive thinking; thinking tokens bill at $25/MTok and NOTHING on disk measures them — the harness files capture only the visible JSON. The claude-api skill's cost guidance says effort is the first quality-trading lever and that lower effort on current models often matches higher effort on prior ones. Is `high` load-bearing for the Scribe, or an untested constant of the kind the owner's 08-27 hazard note warns about?

WHY IS THE 1-HOUR TTL RIGHT? The design pins `ttl: '1h'` (2× write) on the block brief. The TOWN block is read by ~10 tab calls seconds apart, where a 5-minute TTL at 1.25× would do — and the caching doc says a 1h TTL "needs at least three requests" to pay off and "buys nothing" for requests under five minutes apart. Nobody has separated the two blocks' TTLs.

IS DAILY LIFE A SECOND CACHE PREFIX? `daily_life/brief.md` is 98,480 chars against every other tab's 96,795 — a different prefix, hence a second 24.6 K-token cache WRITE per hour on top of the main brief. Was that intended, or should the daily-life register live inside the one shared brief so the cache is written once?

DOES THE PRODUCT'S TIER-1 READER RIDE THE CACHE? Ruling 31 and RUN 3's finding 5 say the checklist rides the same cached blocks in the product; the harness's `tier1-*.md` is self-contained and re-embeds the town. If the built `scribe-render` sends it the harness's way, tier 1 roughly doubles the bill. This is a code question nobody has answered and a live-run question the key would settle.

SIX TABS OR TEN? Design §6 costs "six tab calls" and §5c rule 4 calls daily life "a SEVENTH"; the built `firingTabs` walks `SCRIBE_TABS` (thirteen tabs, ~ten firing on the pinned town). Which is the design's intent — and does the proposal price ten or trim the tab set?

THE DAILY CAP: DOES THE OWNER BELIEVE ONE EXISTS? The 13:2x directive says "the daily cap … [is] re-decided inside that design", but no cap was ever designed, ruled or built — it appears only in one chair memory sentence that seems to have read a render cap out of `saveLimit: 3`. The proposal should either surface this as a chair error or propose a cap deliberately; it should not silently inherit one.

WHAT HAPPENS TO THE TIER WHEN THE CORPUS LANDS? The 08:5x end state is that a finished corpus makes the free tier truly free and the Scribe "moves to a HIGHER PAID TIER"; 13:2x says the corpus is every subscription's prose "until the full rewrite is finished" — and the rewrite is PAUSED on the owner's 12:05 word ("focus solely on the scribe"). Is the Scribe tier priced for the world where the corpus is unfinished, the world where it is finished, or both?

THE FREE FIRST RENDER, RE-OPENED. Ruling 2 (one per ACCOUNT, migration-118 pattern) is BUILT in migration 202 but explicitly re-decided by 13:2x. Inside a subscription tier is the right free sample a render per account, a trial epoch, a single free settlement, or nothing at all?

GALLERY VISIBILITY IS A TIER QUESTION. Ruling 3 hides Scribe prose from every gallery viewer fail-closed and schedules the re-open "at W5" — the same wave as the tier. If a subscriber's rendered prose is invisible to everyone else, the tier has no shop window; if it is visible, non-subscribers read paid prose for free. Undecided.

BYOK AS THE ZERO-COGS ARM. Ruling 10 runs a BYOK user's Scribe on their key, and Surveyor already sells BYOK at $14.99/mo with a zero managed allowance. Should the Scribe tier be BYOK-first (near-zero COGS, a real price ceiling problem) or managed-first (COGS-bound)? The record contains the mechanism and no decision.

THE BLIND READ THE DECISION RULE REQUIRES HAS NEVER HAPPENED. Design §10 gates the ship on "a 40-unit blind read: the owner and one Fable seat, Scribe vs corpus, same pools, shuffled" AND a post-refute FAIL rate at or below the corpus's audited defect rate. Five simulated runs measured the instruments; nobody has measured whether the OWNER prefers the prose. Should the tier proposal be written before that read, or should the read be the proposal's first ask?
